external_source: Re-DocRED (MIT, tonytan48) re-labelling DocRED (MIT, THUNLP), Wikipedia-derived; relation labels from the Wikidata API (CC0). Staged by scripts/stage_redocred.py — 100 docs, 3655 gold triplets, 93 relation types.

smoke_run.note: Plumbing validation, not a reference run. Zero failed LLM calls on a 93-relation ontology; 120/120 mention spans quote the source exactly. The not-in-text guard dropped 15 of 46 candidate triplets (~33%) as unsupported — those would otherwise be silent hallucinations carrying provenance. Local model is a weak relation extractor at this ontology size: it anchors on the document subject and attaches everything to it.

ceiling.note: DocRED ships tokenised sentences; text is a space-join, so ~2.4% of gold names do not occur verbatim. Extraction natives drop anything not found verbatim, so this is the benchmark ceiling, not extractor error.

methodology.scoring: Exact case-insensitive (doc_id, head, relation, tail) match. Entity resolution NOT applied before scoring, so alias variants count as misses and recall is a lower bound. Gold is document-level and includes inferred/cross-sentence facts that chunk-local extraction cannot reach by construction.
